record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Is there a meaningful notion of a catalytic data structure, or any genuine benefit to storing a data structure in catalytic memory that must be restored after use?

evidence.quote: Problem 31. Is there a meaningful notion of a catalytic data structure, or is there anything to be gained from a data structure stored in catalytic memory?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In the model of catalytic computation, a Turing machine is equipped with two work tapes: a clean work tape of small size s(n), and a much larger auxiliary tape of size c(n) (the catalytic tape) which is initialized with an arbitrary string τ ∈ {0,1}^{c(n)}. The machine may read and write the catalytic tape freely during its computation, but on every input x and every initial content τ, when the computation halts the catalytic tape must be restored to its original content τ. The class CSPACE(s,c) consists of languages decidable in this model, and catalytic logspace CL = CSPACE(O(log n), 2^{O(log n)}). The catalytic-memory model is known to allow surprising algorithmic gains over ordinary space-bounded computation when computing functions.

A data structure in this context would be a representation D(S) of a set or object S, stored on the catalytic tape, that supports a collection of query operations (and possibly updates), where each operation is carried out by a catalytic procedure: it reads from D(S), uses a small clean workspace, may temporarily modify the catalytic tape (including the region holding D(S)), but at the end of the operation must leave the catalytic tape exactly as it was at the start. Standard data-structure parameters (space, query time, update time, preprocessing) are measured with respect to this restoration requirement.

Problem. Formulate a meaningful and non-trivial notion of a "catalytic data structure" in the sense above, and determine whether there exists any data-structuring task — for example dictionary lookup, predecessor search, dynamic connectivity, range queries, or any other natural problem — for which storing the data structure in catalytic memory (subject to the restoration constraint) yields a genuine quantitative advantage in space and/or operation time compared to what is achievable by ordinary (non-catalytic) data structures of comparable resources. Either exhibit such a problem together with a catalytic data structure achieving a provable improvement, or prove that no such advantage is possible under a suitable model.
artifact.status_search_result: Catalytic computation remains an active research area, with focus on complexity classes like CL and CNL rather than data structures. No published results were found proposing or refuting a notion of "catalytic data structure" yielding genuine benefits from storing structures in catalytic memory; the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Catalytic computation studies space-bounded computation with an additional large auxiliary tape that must be restored; open problems include extending the model to data structures.
status_evidence.claim: No known notion of catalytic data structure with proven advantage is reported.
